questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which two diseases are the types of variable vessel vasculitis on the title page?
questions.exp: Variable vessel vasculitis types are Behcet disease and Cogan syndrome. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Behcet disease was previously classified under what category in the source?
questions.exp: The Behcet section notes it was previously classified under large-vessel vasculitis. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which Takayasu-versus-Behcet contrast is printed?
opts: Both have identical granulomatous lymphocytic lesions
Behcet is always necrotizing with RBC extravasation
Takayasu: panarteritis with lymphocytes and granulomas; Behcet: panarteritis with non-necrotizing inflammation, panniculitis, obliterative phlebitis, neutrophils and no granulomas
Takayasu: neutrophils and no granulomas; Behcet: lymphocytes and granulomas
questions.exp: The comparison table lists Takayasu panarteritis with lymphocyte predominance and granulomas, while Behcet has panarteritis, non-necrotizing inflammation without fibrinoid necrosis/RBC extravasation, panniculitis, obliterative phlebitis, neutrophils and absent granulomas. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which condition is a differential diagnosis for obliterative phlebitis?
questions.exp: The note states differential diagnosis for obliterative phlebitis is IgG4 disease. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which disease is listed under arteritis without granuloma rather than arteritis with granuloma?
questions.exp: The arteritis-without-granuloma column lists Behcet disease and MPA; the granuloma column lists large-vessel vasculitis, GPA, EGPA, rheumatoid vasculitis and Cogan syndrome. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which HLA is highlighted as associated with Behcet disease?
questions.exp: Risk factors list HLA-B51 as associated with Behcet disease, with other HLA-A26, HLA-B27 and HLA-B57. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which pathophysiology and immune-cell pattern is printed for Behcet disease?
opts: T-cell mediated inflammation with Th1 greater than Th17
questions.exp: Pathophysiology is T-cell mediated inflammation, Th1 greater than Th17. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which antibodies/factors are expressed in Behcet disease according to the source?
opts: ASCA, anti-selenium binding protein, anti-enolase, MICA gene and ER aminopeptidase
questions.exp: Factors expressed include ASCA antibody, anti-selenium binding protein, anti-enolase, MICA gene and ER aminopeptidase. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: What note links ASCA in Behcet disease to Crohn disease?
opts: ASCA is also found in Crohn disease, so GIT manifestations are similar
ASCA is a marker of renal disease only
ASCA is diagnostic of Cogan syndrome
questions.exp: The note states ASCA antibody is also found in Crohn disease and GIT manifestations are similar. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which clinical profile is printed for Behcet disease?
opts: Most affected age 30–50, severe in young males, chronic relapsing multisystem autoimmune disease
Most affected age below 5, self-limiting only
Age above 70 with only shoulder stiffness
questions.exp: Behcet disease most affected age group is 30–50 years, severe disease occurs in young males and it is chronic relapsing multisystem autoimmune disease. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which system is specifically spared in Behcet disease?
questions.exp: The clinical manifestations line explicitly states Behcet spares the kidney. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which note lists pulmonary artery vasculitis/aneurysm in two diseases?
questions.exp: The note says pulmonary artery vasculitis/aneurysm is seen in Takayasu arteritis and Behcet disease. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Under the International Criteria for Behcet disease, what score establishes diagnosis?
questions.exp: The International criteria column states diagnosis is established by score ≥4. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: In the International Criteria table, which manifestations score 2 points each?
opts: Oral aphthosis, genital aphthosis and ocular lesions
Skin lesion, neurologic manifestation and vascular manifestation
questions.exp: The table assigns 2 points each to oral aphthosis, genital aphthosis and ocular lesions. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which oral-ulcer statement is printed for Behcet disease?
opts: Oral ulcers heal with scarring and spare lips
Oral ulcers are never used for diagnosis
Mandatory/pathognomonic recurrent painful ulcers at least 3 times/year at lips, buccal mucosa, tongue or soft palate
questions.exp: Oral aphthous ulcers are mandatory/pathognomonic, recurrent ≥3 times/year painful ulcers, commonly at lips, buccal mucosa, tongue and soft palate. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which note is printed while evaluating oral ulcers in Behcet disease?
opts: Always diagnose SLE if ulcers are painful
Rule out HIV during diagnosis of ulcer
questions.exp: The page notes to rule out HIV during diagnosis of ulcer. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which genital-ulcer feature is least compatible with Behcet disease in the source?
opts: Spares scrotum and labia as the most common sites
More deeply situated and more painful
Less recurrent and heals with scarring
questions.exp: Behcet genital ulcers most commonly involve scrotum and labia; they are deep, painful, less recurrent, heal with scarring and spare glans penis/urethra. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: How is a positive pathergy test performed and read in the source?
opts: Oblique skin puncture with a 25-gauge needle; papule/pustule with erythema after 24–48 hours
Venepuncture with 18-gauge needle; halo sign immediately
questions.exp: Pathergy test is hypersensitivity to long scratch/intradermal saline injection, oblique skin puncture using a 25-gauge needle, with papule/pustule and erythema after 24–48 hours. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: What sensitivity and specificity are printed for the pathergy test?
questions.exp: The pathergy test is described as low sensitivity 60% and high specificity 80%. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which cutaneous manifestation is most common in Behcet disease?
questions.exp: Cutaneous manifestations include all types of skin lesions and list papulopustular lesions as most common. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which note about erythema nodosum in sarcoidosis is printed?
opts: Painful pretibial pigmented papule is specific to sarcoid
It is never seen in sarcoidosis
questions.exp: The note states erythema nodosum in sarcoidosis has all P's except pigmentation. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which ophthalmic table contrast is correct?
opts: Both have chronic relapsing bilateral panuveitis; Behcet also has retinal vasculitis and hypopyon with PC > AC
Sarcoidosis has hypopyon and PC > AC; Behcet has AC > PC only
questions.exp: Ophthalmic table: characteristic feature is chronic relapsing bilateral panuveitis; Behcet has retinal vasculitis and hypopyon, and chamber involvement PC > AC, while sarcoidosis has AC > PC. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which joint manifestation is printed for Behcet disease?
questions.exp: Behcet joint manifestation is asymmetrical non-erosive oligoarthritis. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Which warning-sign set is listed for Behcet disease?
opts: Renal RPGN, pulmonary cavities and saddle nose only
Jaw claudication and optic disc pallor only
Vascular thrombosis, GI involvement resembling Crohn, CNS involvement and very rare cardiac disease
questions.exp: Warning signs include vascular thrombosis, GI involvement resembling Crohn disease, CNS involvement and very rare cardiac involvement. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Behcet CNS involvement is under the influence of which cytokine, and which types are listed?
opts: IL-6; vascular, parenchymal and brainstem encephalitis
questions.exp: CNS involvement is under influence of IL-6 and types listed are vascular, parenchymal and brainstem encephalitis. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: Sweet syndrome is described how in Behcet disease?
opts: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis only seen in Behcet
A chronic lymphocytic panniculitis seen only in Takayasu
questions.exp: Sweet syndrome is acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis and is stated to be only seen in Behcet. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
questions.q: What is MAGIC syndrome in the source?
opts: Mouth and genital ulcers with inflamed cartilage: Behcet plus relapsing polychondritis
questions.exp: MAGIC syndrome is mouth and genital ulcers with inflamed cartilage, a combination of Behcet disease and relapsing polychondritis. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
questions.q: How is Behcet disease diagnosed in the source?
opts: It requires renal biopsy in every case
questions.exp: Diagnosis section states it is a clinical diagnosis. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
questions.q: Which skin-lesion and immunoglobulin findings are printed for Behcet diagnosis?
opts: Predominantly neutrophilic cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis with mixed IgG/IgM/C3 infiltrate
Pure eosinophilic necrosis with no immunoglobulins
questions.exp: Skin lesions are predominantly neutrophilic with cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis; immunoglobulins are mixed infiltrate IgG/IgM/C3. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
questions.q: Which treatment is printed for mucocutaneous Behcet disease?
opts: Oral steroid plus MMF for every patient
Steroid plus antiviral plus plasma exchange
questions.exp: The treatment table lists mucocutaneous disease as topical steroid plus PGE2 gel. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
questions.q: Which treatment is printed for severe mucocutaneous Behcet disease?
opts: Thalidomide plus methotrexate plus topical steroid
Topical steroid plus PGE2 gel only
questions.exp: Severe mucocutaneous disease treatment is thalidomide plus methotrexate plus topical steroid. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
questions.q: Which systemic Behcet treatment statement is printed?
opts: Topical PGE2 only for systemic disease
No treatment because disease is always self-limiting
Oral prednisolone plus methotrexate or MMF, with MMF for more severe and methotrexate for less severe disease
questions.exp: Systemic treatment includes oral steroid prednisolone plus methotrexate or MMF; more severe disease uses MMF and less severe uses methotrexate. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
questions.q: Which age group is printed for Cogan syndrome?
questions.exp: Cogan syndrome age group is 20–30 years. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
questions.q: What characteristic triad defines Cogan syndrome in the source?
opts: Aortitis, interstitial keratitis and vestibulitis with SNHL similar to Meniere disease within less than 2 years
Oral aphthae, genital ulcers and pathergy
questions.exp: The Cogan triad shows aortitis, interstitial keratitis and vestibulitis with sensorineural hearing loss similar to Meniere disease, with less than 2 years shown between ocular and vestibular components. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
questions.q: Which clinical manifestations are listed for Cogan syndrome?
questions.exp: Cogan clinical manifestations include fever with systemic manifestations and gaze-induced nystagmus. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
questions.q: Sensorineural hearing loss in the Cogan section is also seen in which disease?
questions.exp: The note says SNHL is also seen in Wegener granulomatosis. (Book p518)

units.title: 1. Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
units.sec: Behcet disease classification, criteria and manifestations
units.guide:
Variable-vessel vasculitis types lead into Behcet's comparison with Takayasu and granuloma tables.
Risk factors, T-cell pathophysiology, antibodies and multisystem manifestations are preserved.
Diagnostic criteria, oral/genital/pathergy/cutaneous/ocular/joint/warning signs follow source order.

units.title: 2. Diagnosis, treatment and Cogan syndrome
units.guide:
Behcet diagnosis remains clinical with neutrophilic skin lesions and mixed immunoglobulin infiltrate.
Treatment is separated into mucocutaneous, severe mucocutaneous and systemic disease.
Cogan syndrome age, triad, manifestations and SNHL note close the chapter.
